question.:question/problem:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y-8z &=-12 \\ -2x+5y+18z &=27.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -8 & -12 \\ -2 & 5 & 18 & 27\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -8 & -12 \\ -2 & 5 & 18 & 27\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -8 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -4 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-4z &=-6 \\ y+2z &=3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=4z-6 \\ y &=-2z+3 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4z-6 \\ -2z+3 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=-5 \\ (k+6)y &=-20.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=-6,$ then the second equation is $0=-20,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=-6.$

The system is now

question.:question/problem:
Given that $A,B,$ and $C$ are $3\times 3$ matrices, and  ${I}_{3}$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix, which of the following statements are always true?

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $AB=A{I}_{3}B$
- **II.** $A(B+{I}_{3})=AB$
- **III.** ${I}_{3}A=A{I}_{3}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's consider the statements one by one.

- Statement I is true. Matrix multiplication is associative, so $A{I}_{3}B=(A{I}_{3})B=AB.$

- Statement II is false. Matrix multiplication is distributive, so $A(B+{I}_{3})=AB+A{I}_{3}=AB+A.$ However,  $AB+A\ne AB,$ in general.

- Statement III is true. Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general, however, multiplication by the identity matrix is always commutative. In this case, we have  ${I}_{3}A=A{I}_{3}.$

Therefore, only statements I and III are true.
